#en: Funny how the story keeps changing, depending who is telling it and how close they are to a docking bay. First time I heard it, over watered whiskey in the mess, it was just a rumor about a liner that came apart mid jump, no names, no blame, just a bad roll of the grav dice. Next station over, the same tale had a villain, some engineer who signed off on cheap steel and vanished into the black. After that, I kept hearing about a shadow on the docks, a quiet tech who slipped aboard at night and fixed what the staryards pretended not to see.\n\nToday I ended up in that crooked little Freestar trailer at the edge of the pad, listening to a deputy whose hands shook just a little when they scrolled through failure reports. Same incidents, same ship classes, same manufacturer tags, but the way they talked about it was different: not curses, not campfire stories, just a pattern no one higher up wanted to acknowledge. They say the masked fixer is a saboteur in one port, a savior in another. The only thing that does not change is the silence whenever someone asks why the same hulls keep cracking in the same way and why the logs keep getting buried under other case numbers.
zh: 有趣的是，这故事总在变，取决于讲它的人是谁、离泊位有多近。我第一次听到它，是在食堂里就着掺水的威士忌——那只是个关于一艘班轮在跃迁途中解体的传言，没有名字，没有归罪，只是重力骰子掷了个坏点数。到了隔壁空间站，同一个故事里有了反派，某个签了廉价钢材的字、然后消失在黑暗里的工程师。再往后，我一直听说码头上有个影子，一名安静的技工夜里溜上船，修好那些造船厂假装没看见的东西。\n\n今天我最后待在泊位边缘那间歪歪扭扭的自由星系联盟拖车里，听一名副手说话——他滚动事故报告时，手抖得有一点点明显。同样的事件、同样的船级、同样的制造商标签，可他们谈起它的方式不一样：不是咒骂，不是篝火故事，而是一个更高层没人愿意承认的图案。他们说那个蒙面修理工在一个港口是破坏者，在另一个港口是救世主。唯一不变的是沉默——每当有人问，为什么同样的船壳老是以同样的方式开裂，为什么日志总是被埋在别的案号底下。

#en:
I am writing this down so I will not start believing the official version.

We were three ships running ore and machine parts toward HopeTown, nothing fancy, same corridor I have flown since before the Armistice. UC traffic pings in a correction, minor variance, cleaner path through the junk belt. I swear I checked the vector twice. Looked safe. Then we caught the echo of a wreck ahead that should not have been there, hull still warm on thermals, cargo already stripped clean. Somebody had got the tip before us rode the same correction, just a few hours earlier.

Afterward, in the bar at New Atlantis, the story turned into one more spacer tale bad luck, old charts, UC underfunding. The captains laughed it off, but when the drinks thinned out, they started whispering about a voice that sounds like ops, numbers that never show in the logs. Every time the rumor cooled, some tug limped in with a new near miss and the same quiet pattern, like the story is trying to die and keeps getting dragged back up by people who cannot unsee their own telemetry. I am no investigator. I just know my ship went exactly where I was told to go, and someone was already there, waiting.
zh:
我把这个写下来，好让自己不至于开始相信官方的说法。

我们三艘船正朝希望镇运送矿石和机器零件，没什么特别的，还是那条我自停战之前就在飞的走廊。联殖交通台传来一条修正，小偏差，一条穿过垃圾带的更干净路径。我发誓我把矢量核对过两遍。看着很安全。然后我们捕捉到前方一艘残骸的回响，那本不该在那里，船体在热成像上还是温的，货物已经被清得干干净净。有人比我们更早拿到消息，走了同样的修正，只不过早了几个小时。

事后在新亚特兰蒂斯的酒吧里，这故事又变成了一则太空人的传说——运气不好、旧星图、联殖经费不足。船长们一笑而过，可酒一喝淡，他们就开始低声说起一个听起来像作战部的声音、一些从不出现在日志里的数字。每次传言冷却，就有某艘拖船带着一次新的险情和一成不变的安静图案跛行归来，像这故事想要死去，却一直被那些无法对自己遥测视而不见的人拖回来。我不是调查员。我只知道我的船完全去了被告知要去的地方，而有人早已在那里等着。

#en: I am writing this in the dark between shifts, because the ship feels wrong and I do not trust the official logs to remember that. We were not supposed to break route this close to Neon. Manifest said standard haul, no deviations, but the Trade Authority dispatcher slipped in a new vector at the last minute, barely a line of explanation. The bridge took it anyway. Credits make people move faster than they should. Now the Skyclipper hums unevenly, like the Grav core is holding its breath, and half the nav data from the last jump came through smeared, as if the stars themselves dragged. Ivy tried to scrub the errors, muttering that it was just interference from traffic around Volii, but I saw the look she gave that corrupted segment, like it was something alive. Someone pushed this course in a hurry, then turned their eyes away from what it might brush against. Out on a survey outpost we found the first stray blackbox, just a fragment. Then there were those odd beacon returns in high orbit, callsigns that matched ships marked as lost, and now this cargo run with its quiet addendum and a route line that bends closer to Neon's shadows than any normal hauler would risk.
zh: 我在两个班次之间的黑暗里写下这些，因为这艘船感觉不对劲，而我不信任官方日志会记得这一点。我们本不该在离霓虹城这么近的地方脱离航线。清单说是标准运输，不作偏离，可贸易管理局的调度员在最后一刻塞进了一条新矢量，解释只有寥寥一行。舰桥还是接了。信用币让人动得比该动的快。如今天剪号的嗡鸣变得不均匀，像重力核在屏住呼吸，而上次跃迁的导航数据有一半传过来时是糊的，仿佛星星本身被拖了一道。艾薇试着清洗那些错误，嘟囔说那只是沃利星周边交通的干扰，可我看见她看那截损坏数据时的表情，像那是活的东西。有人匆忙推上这条航线，然后把目光从它可能擦到的东西上移开。在一座勘测前哨站，我们找到了第一只游离的黑匣子，只是一个碎片。接着是高层轨道上那些奇怪的信标回波，呼号对得上被标记为失踪的飞船；如今又是这趟带着安静附件的货运，航线朝霓虹城的阴影弯得比任何正常货船敢冒险的程度都近。

#en: I am recording this quietly, because people who talk too loud about lanes and disappearances stop getting invited back on good contracts. Learned that the hard way at a bar outside HopeTown two months ago. I mentioned a transport that never pinged its arrival beacon, and three captains suddenly remembered somewhere else they had to be. The fourth just stared into his drink and told me, very carefully, that the frontier eats ships and stories the same way.\n\nToday I put down on an old relay they swore was decommissioned. No traffic, no maintenance drones, just a dead lattice hanging where three routes used to meet. Inside, the boards are burned but not empty; you can still see faint traces of jumps that do not match any published corridor. Someone carved their own path through here, again and again, so clean the drives barely left a bruise. I mentioned that pattern once to a LIST clerk I know, and watched her face close up like an airlock. She changed the subject to fuel prices and never answered my messages after. Out here, everyone has noticed something wrong in the map, but the smart ones keep their opinions small, like they are afraid the vacuum might be listening.
zh: 我悄悄地录下这些，因为那些把航道和失踪事件说得太响的人，就不会再被邀请接好合同了。两个月前在希望镇外的一间酒吧里，我吃一堑长一智。我提到一艘从未发出抵达信标的运输船，三个船长忽然想起他们别处还有事。第四个只是盯着自己的酒，非常谨慎地告诉我：边疆吃掉飞船和故事的方式是一样的。\n\n今天我降落在一座他们赌咒说已退役的旧中继站上。没有交通，没有维护无人机，只有一副死掉的格架悬在三条航线曾经交汇的地方。里面，主板烧了但并不空；你仍能看见些微的跃迁痕迹，不属于任何公布过的走廊。有人在这里一遍又一遍地凿出自己的路，干净得驱动几乎没留下一块淤青。我曾向一个我认识的独立盟文员提起那个图案，眼看着她脸像气闸一样合上了。她把话题转到了燃料价格上，此后就再没回过我的消息。在这外面，人人都注意到地图上有什么不对，可聪明人都把自己的看法压得很小，像他们害怕真空可能在偷听。

#en:
Hard to say when it started feeling inevitable. Maybe back on that rock out past the lanes, when I cracked open a discarded slate and saw numbers that did not belong to any homestead that size. Maybe in Gagarin, watching freight hands swear a shipment existed while the manifest swore it did not. Either way, it brought me here.

The Fundrunner is dead metal outside, but inside you can still feel the hum of old credit flows, like a ghost current under your boots. GalBank stamped their logo everywhere, as if repetition makes trust. It does not. Every sealed rack I pass smells like another story that ended the same way: someone in the black, someone in the ground.

The trail says whoever taught her how to cut debts loose used ships like this as a pulpit. Phantom yields at an extraction site that should be dry, families whose ledgers just blinked clean, a pattern of erased risk that always arcs back toward Helium-3 and quiet corridors like these. I followed rumors from a forgotten outpost to noisy docks, from there to this drifting vault, and every step made it clearer this was never random; the numbers were always steering me toward the plants that feed the whole game.
zh:
很难说它是什么时候开始显得无可避免的。也许是在航道外那块岩石上，我撬开一块被丢弃的数据板，看见一些不属于那么大规模农庄的数字。也许是在加加林，看着运货人手赌咒说一批货存在，而清单却赌咒说不存在。不管怎样，它把我带到了这里。

资金行者号外面是死金属，可里面你仍能感觉到旧信贷流动的嗡鸣，像靴子底下一道幽灵电流。银河银行到处都盖着他们的标志，仿佛重复就能造出信任。可它造不出。我路过的每一个密封机架，闻起来都像另一个以同样方式结束的故事：有人在太空里，有人在地底下。

痕迹表明，教她如何把债务解绑的人，用的就是这类飞船当布道台。一座本该枯竭的采掘点却有幽灵般的产量、账本忽然眨眼变干净的家庭、一种总是绕回氦-3和像这样的安静走廊的被抹去的风险图案。我顺着传言从一座被遗忘的前哨站追到嘈杂的码头，再从那追到这艘漂流的金库船；每一步都更清楚地说明，这从不是随机的；那些数字一直在把我引向喂养整场博弈的暗桩。

#en:
Everybody swears they heard it from someone else first.

The deserter whose bunk I borrowed said a friend in SysDef mentioned it over cards. The tech running the power in this rusted hide said it came down from some analyst on Jemison. I am sitting in the dark with the last of the juice running through an old overwatch console, and no one will admit they were the one who actually saw it.

Thing is, I have seen it now.

Buried three layers down under scrubbed patrol logs, there is a jump trace that does not fit any sanctioned corridor. The ship on that feed slides between pings, just outside where the net is supposed to be solid, like it knows exactly where the blind spots live. Every time it reappears, its vector lines kiss the same set of coordinates orbiting Deepala. The Clinic.

People say that station sees everything the war broke and everything the lanes keep breaking still. If he is sampling the damage his numbers do, that is where he would go to listen. I have got the timestamp, the entry window, and the angle his drive flared when he dropped into local space. It is not much, but it is the first time this ghost leaves the same fingerprint in two different systems.
zh:
人人都赌咒说自己是先从别人那儿听来的。

我借了他铺位的那名逃兵说，联殖防务的一个朋友打牌时提起过。给这处锈蚀藏身处供电的技工说，那是从杰米森某个分析师那儿传下来的。我坐在黑暗里，靠着流经一台旧监视控制台的最后一格电，而没人肯承认自己才是真正看见过它的那个。

问题是，如今我看见了。

在三层被擦洗过的巡逻日志底下，有一段不属于任何获批走廊的跃迁痕迹。那数据流里的飞船在探测之间滑动，刚好在本该密实的网络之外，像它清楚知道盲区住在哪里。每次它重新出现，它的矢量线都亲上同一组环绕迪帕拉运转的坐标。星际诊所号。

人们说那座空间站见证了战争毁掉的一切，也见证着航道仍在不断毁掉的一切。如果他在采集自己那些数字造成的损伤，那正是他回去偷听的地方。我拿到了时间戳、进入窗口，以及他切入本地空间时驱动喷焰的角度。这些不算多，可这是这个幽灵第一次在两个不同的星系里留下同一枚指纹。

#en:
I keep telling myself this is just another relay job, just another Trade Authority courier drifting between people who pretend they are not on the same side. The hull hums like always, life support purrs, the recycler coughs every few hours. Familiar noises. Comforting, until you notice the other sounds.

Tonight I heard the ship talk to no one.

Old UC diagnostic routines, buried deep in the nav core, spun up during downtime. Their pings went out into the dark, calling to beacons that were supposed to be decommissioned years ago. No one on the manifest ordered that. The captain shrugged, said legacy code sometimes ghosts the system. But I watched the patterns scroll by and they were too clean, too deliberate, like somebody had been tuning them while we ran cargo and looked the other way.

We docked at a rock last week, quiet place, barely a name. A freelancer handed over a data packet, eyes flicking to the stars every other breath, muttering about ships that arrive late or not at all. Since then, the old routines have been waking more often, pointing toward the same patch of sky. The pay on this route is better than it should be. Everyone pretends not to notice that, either.
zh:
我一直告诉自己，这不过是又一次中继任务，又一艘在假装彼此不在同一边的人之间漂流的贸易管理局快船。船体像往常一样嗡鸣，生命维持系统轻声运转，回收机每隔几小时咳一声。熟悉的声响。让人安心，直到你注意到别的声响。

今晚我听见这艘船在对无人说话。

深埋在导航核心里的旧联殖诊断程序，在闲置时段转了起来。它们的探测发进黑暗，呼叫那些多年前就该退役的信标。清单上没人下过这道命令。船长耸耸肩，说是遗留代码偶尔会在这套系统里闹鬼。可我看着那些图案滚过，它们太干净、太刻意了，像有人趁我们运货、别过头去的时候一直在调校它们。

上周我们停靠在一块岩石上，安静的地方，几乎连名字都没有。一个自由职业者递来一份数据包，眼睛每隔一次呼吸就往星空瞟，嘟囔着那些迟到或者根本不到的飞船。从那以后，那些旧程序醒得越来越频繁，指向同一片天空。这条航线的报酬比它该有的高。这一点大家也假装没注意到。

#en:
I am sitting in a dead relay, listening to ghosts that never got the memo war is over.

The main board is red-lit and half the panels are fused, but when I tied a microcell into the backbone, the grid woke up like it had just been on break. Old patrol routines, still cycling after all these years, quietly logging every shuttle and ore hauler that screamed past the no-fly line. Nobody checked, nobody cared, so the system kept watching.

Buried under a decade of dust and recycled timestamps, I found it  a set of atmospheric returns that did not match any filed transponder, cutting through restricted airspace like they owned it. The pattern is clean, too clean for a smuggler guessing blind. Whoever plotted that path knew every blind arc in the grid and trusted the forgotten software to still be doing its job. I piggybacked the trajectory into orbitals and there it was, a residual signature stitched into traffic corrections around a processing hub hanging over the planet.  

So now I know where the next piece is waiting, caught in the same old procedures that outlived their operators. The brass turned their eyes away, but the machines never stopped watching, and she gambled on that.
zh:
我坐在一座死掉的中继站里，听着那些从没收到战争结束通知的鬼。

主板亮着红光，一半面板已熔接，可当我把一块微电池接进主干线时，整个电网就像刚休完假一样醒了过来。老旧的巡逻程序，这么多年后仍在循环，悄悄记录着每一架尖叫着冲过禁飞线的穿梭机和矿石货船。没人检查，没人在意，于是系统就一直看着。

埋在十年的灰尘和循环时间戳底下，我找到了它——一组不符合任何申报应答器的大气回波，切开受限空域，像那地方是它们家的。那图案很干净，干净得不像是靠瞎猜的走私贩。画下那条路径的人，知道网格里每一道盲弧，并且信任那套被遗忘的软件仍在干着自己的活。我把那条轨迹搭进轨道层，它就在那儿——一个残余特征，缝在一座悬在这颗行星上方处理枢纽周边的交通修正里。

所以现在我知道下一块碎片在哪儿等着了，卡在那些比操作员活得还久的旧程序里。高层把目光移开了，可机器从未停止监视，而她赌的就是这一点。

#en: I am writing this from the corner of the trailer, back to the bulkhead so I can see the door. The deputy went out for "fresh air," which is funny given the dust, and left their board on idle. They think I do not notice where their eyes slide whenever the subject comes up, how the room goes quiet when someone mentions that engineer in anything louder than a mutter. Nobody wants to be the one on record knowing too much.\n\nStill, patterns are hard to unsee once you trace them. Every jump failure, every emergency dock closure, every "miracle" overnight repair the deputy flagged sits on the same crooked line. The last report they filed, buried under a different case number, mentions a disposal site Deimos supposedly cleared years ago. Same prefix code on the ship that limped in last month with stress fractures on a frame that was "well within spec." They circled those coordinates twice, then closed the file without sending it. That is how I know it matters. The people closest to whatever happened will not meet my eyes when I ask about old scrapyards, and one of them quietly told me to avoid that sector if I valued my hull. Which is exactly why I logged the location before the board timed out.
zh: 我在拖车角落里写下这些，背靠着舱壁，这样我能看见门。那副手出去"透口气"了——考虑到这满天的灰，这说法挺好笑——把板子留在闲置状态。他们以为我没注意到，每当话题一提起，他们的目光就滑向哪里；有人用比嘟囔大一点的声音提起那位工程师时，房间如何安静下来。没人想成为那个被记录下知道太多的人。\n\n不过，图案一旦被你描出来，就很难再当没看见。每一次跃迁失败、每一次紧急封港、每一次副手标记的"奇迹般"的连夜修复，都落在同一条歪曲的线上。他们归档的最后一份报告，埋在另一个案号底下，提到一处据称火卫二多年前就清理过的处置场。上个月跛行进来的那艘船用的是同样的前缀代码，其框架上带着应力裂纹，而框架"完全符合规格"。他们把那些坐标圈了两次，然后没发送就结了案。就是这样我才知道它要紧。跟那些最接近真相的人打听旧废料场时，他们都不肯对上我的眼睛，其中一个还悄悄告诉我，要是珍惜自己的船壳，就避开那个星区。正因为如此，我在板子超时之前把位置记了下来。
